title: Finding an integration theory for compact p-adic spaces
notes: The heading asks for a reasonable class of \(p\)-adic measures on a compact analytic \(X/K\), with integrals of analytic maps \(X\to L\).
statement: For a finite extension \(L/K/\mathbb Q_p\), a compact zero-dimensional Hausdorff space \(X\), and a bounded finitely additive \(L\)-valued function on clopen subsets, integration extends uniquely from locally constant functions to a continuous \(L\)-linear functional on \(C(X,L)\). Locally analytic integrands also admit larger distribution classes after imposing growth bounds.
reconstruction: Compactness, completeness and boundedness are explicit sufficient hypotheses supplied here; the notebook asks a programme-level question, not uniqueness of an optimal measure class.
fate: \citet[\S8.1 and Theorem~8.6]{manin1973periods}; the concrete answers, rather than an unspecified universal class, are the subject of this exposition.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Adelic Mellin motivation with an unspecified quotient
notes: The notes schematically write \(L(\chi)=\int_{G_A/G_K}\chi\,d\mu\) and identify \(G_K\) with principal adeles.
statement: The record does not specify \(G\), the measure, convergence, or the automorphic test function; no single integral formula is asserted here beyond its role as motivation.
fate: \citet[Introduction and \S1]{manin1976nonarchimedean} supplies a developed adelic framework, but does not identify every missing symbol in this line.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the intended adelic analogy is clear, but this formula is not an independently identifiable theorem.

title: Bernoulli values of the classical zeta function
notes: The displays compare \(\zeta(2m)\) and \(\zeta(1-2m)\) with Bernoulli numbers, with a question mark at the latter sign.
reconstruction: The Bernoulli convention and omitted constants are supplied; divergent power sums are not ordinary convergent sums.
fate: Classical formulas, restated in \citet[\S1 and \S5]{nica2024irrationality}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Gelfand on divergent sums and spectral parity
notes: The parenthetical intervention juxtaposes \(\sum n^3\), Bernoulli numbers and sums of powers of eigenvalues of \(-y^{\prime\prime}+p(x)y=\lambda y\), saying that integers and half-integers differ.
statement: As an ordinary series \(\sum_{n\ge1}n^3\) diverges. Zeta regularization assigns \(\zeta(-3)=1/120\), but a spectral analogue requires an operator domain, boundary conditions and a specified regularization, none of which are recorded.
fate: The Bernoulli identity is classical; \citet[\S1 and \S5]{nica2024irrationality} does not settle the unformulated spectral comparison.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the spectral-parity remark remains insufficiently specified for a problem-index entry.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Removing the Euler factor and interpolating zeta values
notes: The values \((1-p^{2m-1})B_{2m}/(2m)\) are called \(p\)-adically continuous and analytic.
statement: For odd \(p\), interpolation of \(-(1-p^{n-1})B_n/n\) is performed on a fixed residue class of \(n\bmod(p-1)\), with the standard Teichmuller twist. The zeta branch is meromorphic with its pole at \(s=1\); there is no single untwisted analytic function on all of \(\mathbb Z_p\) realizing every even weight without a branch convention.
reconstruction: The sign, branch restriction and pole are indispensable editorial qualifications.
fate: \citet[\S0.1--0.3]{manin1976nonarchimedean} restates the Kubota--Leopoldt construction (1964).
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The proposed cross-prime analytic analogy
notes: The notes suggest that \(\mathbb Q_p\to\mathbb Q_\ell\), \(p\ne\ell\), may be easier than \(\mathbb Q_p\to\mathbb Q_p\), but call it unknown.
statement: Neither the function space nor the regularity condition nor a target theorem is stated. Continuous maps between these totally disconnected fields alone do not specify the intended arithmetic problem.
fate: No exact problem was identified after reading the corresponding integration sections of \citet[\S8]{manin1973periods} and \citet[Introduction]{manin1976nonarchimedean}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: an exploratory analogy, not a precise unresolved conjecture.

title: Serre classification of compact non-Archimedean manifolds
notes: Serre\textquoteright s theorem is \(X\simeq rA^n\), with \(rA^n\simeq r^{\prime}A^n\iff r\equiv r^{\prime}\pmod{q-1}\).
statement: Let \(K\) be a non-Archimedean local field with valuation ring \(A\) and residue cardinality \(q\). For fixed \(n\ge1\), every nonempty compact \(K\)-analytic manifold of pure dimension \(n\) is analytically isomorphic to a finite disjoint union \(rA^n\); the isomorphism invariant is \(i(X)=r\bmod(q-1)\).
reconstruction: The English translation says analytic set, but the Russian abbreviation and scan say analytic manifold. Pure positive dimension and nonemptiness are stated explicitly here.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1 and corollary, p.~409]{serre1965classification}; received March 1964, published 1965.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Computing the Serre invariant by reduction
notes: The notebook asks \ru{Как вычислить} \(r\), then gives \(r(X)=\#X_0(A/\mathfrak m)\) for a smooth scheme over \(A\).
statement: If \(\mathcal X/A\) is smooth, separated and of finite type, with nonempty \(\mathcal X(A)\) of pure relative dimension \(n\ge1\), the inverse image of each residue point in \(\mathcal X(k)\) is an analytic \(n\)-ball. Thus \(i(\mathcal X(A))\equiv\#\mathcal X(k)\pmod{q-1}\).
reconstruction: The integer number of residue discs is one representative of the invariant, not a canonical integer-valued invariant of the analytic manifold.
fate: \citet[example (i), p.~410]{serre1965classification}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The projective line as two analytic balls
notes: The notes count \(q+1\) residue points and obtain two balls; they write \(\mathbb P^1(K)=\mathbb Q_p\cup\{\infty\}\) and \(pA\cup A^{-1}\).
statement: For any non-Archimedean local field \(K\), \(\mathbb P^1(K)=K\cup\{\infty\}\) is the disjoint union of \(\mathfrak m\) and \(\{x:|x|\ge1\}\cup\{\infty\}\); inversion identifies the latter with \(A\). Therefore it is two analytic balls and \(i=2\bmod(q-1)\).
reconstruction: Replace Qp by K and pA by the maximal ideal for ramified extensions; the omitted point at infinity is included in the inverse-coordinate chart.
fate: An explicit instance of \citet[Theorem~1]{serre1965classification}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Compact Lie groups and supernatural order
notes: For a compact \(p\)-adic Lie group the supernatural order is \(p^\infty N\), \((p,N)=1\), followed by \(N=r(X)\) and an \(SL_2\) example.
statement: A positive-dimensional compact \(\mathbb Q_p\)-analytic group has an open pro-\(p\) subgroup and supernatural order \(p^\infty N\) with finite prime-to-\(p\) part \(N\). The analytic invariant is \(i(G)\equiv N\pmod{p-1}\). For \(SL_2(\mathbb Z_p)\), \(N=p^2-1\), so \(i(G)=0\); its representative among \(1,\ldots,p-1\) is \(p-1\).
reconstruction: The invariant is a residue class. The notebook\textquoteright s displayed modulus p in the SL2 example is incompatible with the preceding theorem.
fate: \citet[example (ii), p.~410]{serre1965classification} gives the compact-group application.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Distributions on clopen subsets
notes: An \(L\)-measure is an \(L\)-valued finitely additive function on open-and-closed subsets of compact \(X\).
statement: An \(L\)-valued distribution on a compact totally disconnected Hausdorff space assigns \(\mu(\varnothing)=0\) and \(\mu(U\sqcup V)=\mu(U)+\mu(V)\) for disjoint clopens. It is a bounded measure when \(\sup_U|\mu(U)|_L<\infty\).
reconstruction: Modern terminology distinguishes a possibly unbounded distribution from a bounded measure.
fate: \citet[\S8.1]{manin1973periods}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The residue-class tree and compatibility equation
notes: The tree vertices are clopen sets and \(\mu(a+p^m)=\sum_{b\equiv a\ (p^m)}\mu(b+p^{m+1})\).
statement: For \(X=\mathbb Z_p\), specifying numbers \(\mu_m(a)\in L\) for \(a\in\mathbb Z/p^m\mathbb Z\), \(m\ge0\), subject to \(\mu_m(a)=\sum_{j=0}^{p-1}\mu_{m+1}(a+jp^m)\), determines exactly one clopen distribution.
fate: \citet[\S8.1, equation~(24)]{manin1973periods}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Invariant p-adic distribution is unbounded
notes: Translation-invariant values are \(c p^{-m}\), whose \(p\)-adic absolute values tend to infinity when \(c\ne0\).
statement: The unique translation-invariant distribution on \(\mathbb Z_p\) of total mass \(c\in L\) is \(\mu(a+p^m\mathbb Z_p)=cp^{-m}\). For \(L/\mathbb Q_p\) and \(c\ne0\), it is unbounded and cannot define a continuous functional on all \(C(\mathbb Z_p,L)\).
fate: \citet[\S8.4]{manin1973periods}; already occurrence 1972-298.2.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The bounded two-valued distribution
notes: The values are \(+1\) below \(p^m/2\), \(-1\) above, for unit representatives; the next page asks to check additivity and attributes the measure to Mazur.
statement: For odd \(p\), define on all standard residue classes \(0\le a<p^m\) the value \(+1\) if \(2a<p^m\), and \(-1\) if \(2a>p^m\). Child values sum to the parent value, so this is a bounded distribution; restrict to \(\mathbb Z_p^\times\) if desired.
reconstruction: Odd p excludes an unassigned midpoint and makes 2 a unit. P000505 uses the opposite overall sign.
fate: \citet[\S8.4, regularized distributions]{manin1973periods}; this is a signed normalization of the c=2 construction.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Integration by arbitrary tagged clopen partitions
notes: \(S(f,R)=\sum_i f(a_i)\mu(U_i)\), followed by a limit under refinement.
statement: For a compact \(p\)-adic manifold, take finite disjoint clopen partitions and tags \(a_i\in U_i\); a Riemann integral is the tag-independent limit of these sums as the maximal chart diameter tends to zero, whenever that limit exists.
reconstruction: Disjointness, shrinking mesh and tag independence make the limiting convention explicit.
fate: \citet[\S8.5--8.6]{manin1973periods}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The linear function fails to integrate against the invariant distribution
notes: Canonical sums for \(f(x)=x\), \(\mu(U)=p^{-m}\), tend to \(-1/2\); replacing the representative 0 by \(p^m\) changes the answer.
statement: The canonical level-m sum is \((p^m-1)/2\). Replacing just the tag of \(p^m\mathbb Z_p\) by \(p^m\) adds exactly 1 at every level. The two limits are \(-1/2\) and \(1/2\); hence no tag-independent Riemann integral exists.
reconstruction: The second limiting value is calculated explicitly here. This does not deny the separately defined Volkenborn integral with fixed canonical representatives.
fate: This is the elementary obstruction discussed before \citet[Theorem~8.6]{manin1973periods}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Moderate growth suffices for Lipschitz integration
notes: If \(|\mu(U)/\mu_{\rm inv}(U)|\to0\) and \(f\) is Lipschitz of exponent 1, the integral exists.
statement: Let \(L/\mathbb Q_p\) be finite and \(\mu\) a distribution on \(\mathbb Z_p\). If \(p^{-m}\max_{a\bmod p^m}|\mu(a+p^m\mathbb Z_p)|_p\to0\), every \(L\)-valued Lipschitz function has a tag-independent integral. Finite disjoint unions of charts give the one-dimensional compact-manifold version.
reconstruction: The convergence is uniform over all residue balls; pointwise shrinking alone is not the stated sufficient uniform estimate.
fate: \citet[Theorem~8.6]{manin1973periods}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Repeated Lipschitz integration criterion
notes: The previous theorem is restated for a one-dimensional \(p\)-adic space and a finite extension \(K/\mathbb Q_p\).
statement: For clopen distributions in finitely many \(\mathbb Z_p\)-charts, the uniform condition \(p^{-m}\max_U|\mu(U)|\to0\) guarantees convergence of all tagged sums for Lipschitz integrands.
reconstruction: Uniformity and the finite-chart interpretation are supplied as in item 1973-303.17.
fate: \citet[Theorem~8.6]{manin1973periods}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Moments of the sign distribution
notes: The sign convention is now \(-1\) below the half threshold and \(+1\) above. The displayed odd moments use \((-1)^r(1-2^{-r})B_{r-1}/(2r)\).
statement: For odd \(p\) with this sign convention and standard Bernoulli numbers, \[\int_{\mathbb Z_p}x^k\,d\mu=\frac{(4-2^{1-k})B_{k+1}}{k+1},\qquad k\ge0.\] In particular the total mass is \(-1\), the first moment is \(1/4\), and every positive even moment is zero.
reconstruction: The Bernoulli convention is not defined on this page. The formula here follows from finite power sums, not by silently correcting B indices in the source; see the included exact-arithmetic check.
fate: The underlying regularized distribution is in \citet[\S8.4]{manin1973periods}; the exact normalization displayed here is independently reconstructed from the notebook definition.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Restriction to units produces the Euler factor
notes: \(\int_{\mathbb Z_p^\times}=\int_{\mathbb Z_p}-\int_{p\mathbb Z_p}\), but the displayed exponent changes from \(2r-1\) to \(2m-1\).
statement: The sign distribution satisfies \(\mu(pU)=\mu(U)\). Thus for every integer \(k\ge0\), \(\int_{\mathbb Z_p^\times}x^k\,d\mu=(1-p^k)\int_{\mathbb Z_p}x^k\,d\mu\). At \(k=2r-1\), the factor is \(1-p^{2r-1}\).
reconstruction: The level variable m is replaced by the moment exponent r only in the modern statement.
fate: \citet[\S8.4--8.7]{manin1973periods}; notebook-specific exponents are checked directly.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Continuous character space and its disc coordinates
notes: \(\mathbb Z_p^\times=(\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)^\times\times(1+p)^{\mathbb Z_p}\), and \(\chi_1(1+p)=1+t\).
statement: For odd \(p\) and finite \(K/\mathbb Q_p\), continuous characters of \(\mathbb Z_p^\times\) have a finite Teichmuller component and a component parametrized by \(t\in\mathfrak m_K\) via \(\chi_t((1+p)^a)=(1+t)^a\). For \(p=2\) use \(\{\pm1\}\times(1+4\mathbb Z_2)\) and generator 5.
reconstruction: Continuity, the Teichmuller lift, and the separate p=2 case are made explicit.
fate: \citet[\S8.3]{manin1973periods}; occurrence 1972-299.4 already records the p=2 qualification.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Analyticity of the p-adic Mellin transform
notes: A moderately growing measure has \(\int\chi_{(t)}d\mu=F(t)\in K[[t]]\), convergent for \(|t|<1\).
statement: On each component of character space, the uniform moderate-growth bound on the distribution makes its Mellin transform analytic on the open unit disc of the character parameter. For integer-power characters \(x\mapsto x^n\), fix \(n\bmod(p-1)\) when \(p\) is odd.
fate: \citet[Theorem~8.7]{manin1973periods}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Holomorphic cusp forms for the full modular group
notes: \(P_w\) consists of forms with invariant \(\varphi(z)(dz)^{(w+2)/2}\) and Fourier expansion starting at n=1.
statement: For even \(k=w+2\ge2\), \(S_k(SL_2(\mathbb Z))\) consists of holomorphic functions on the upper half-plane satisfying \(f((az+b)/(cz+d))=(cz+d)^k f(z)\) and vanishing at the cusp; their Fourier expansion is \(\sum_{n\ge1}a_n e^{2\pi inz}\).
fate: \citet[\S1.1--1.2]{manin1973periods}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The discriminant form and low-weight dimensions
notes: The first nonzero space occurs at weight 12, with gaps up to 26 and a parenthetical one-dimensional claim; \(\Delta=q\prod(1-q^n)^{24}\) is displayed.
statement: \(\Delta\in S_{12}(SL_2(\mathbb Z))\), \(S_{12}=\mathbb C\Delta\). The low-weight cusp spaces are zero for even k<12 and for k=14; they have dimension 1 at k=16,18,20,22,26, and dimension 2 at k=24.
reconstruction: The notebook shorthand must not be read as dimension one at every weight from 12 through26; weight24 is the first two-dimensional example.
fate: \citet[\S1.2 and the weight tables in \S7]{manin1973periods}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Hecke eigenbasis and algebraic Fourier coefficients
notes: There is a basis with algebraic-integer coefficients whose Dirichlet series have Euler products.
statement: The commuting Hecke operators on full-level \(S_k\) admit normalized simultaneous eigenforms \(a_1=1\), with coefficients in number fields and algebraic integers; for such a form, \(L(f,s)=\prod_\ell(1-a_\ell\ell^{-s}+\ell^{k-1-2s})^{-1}\) initially in a right half-plane.
reconstruction: Normalized eigenforms, not every arbitrary algebraic basis, give the Euler product. The obscured exponent is resolved by the next clear display on P000507.
fate: \citet[\S1.2 and \S3]{manin1973periods}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The prime Hecke operator and its coefficient recurrence
statement: For \(k=w+2\), this operator preserves \(S_k\) and sends coefficients to \(a_{pn}+p^{k-1}a_{n/p}\), with \(a_{n/p}=0\) unless p divides n. An eigenform obeys \(a_{pn}+p^{k-1}a_{n/p}=a_pa_n\), giving the local quadratic Euler factor.
fate: \citet[\S3, formula~(11)]{manin1973periods}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Rational-cusp period integrals
notes: \(P(x)=\int_x^{i\infty}\Phi(z)dz\) for rational x; it converges at both cusps and \(P(x+1)=P(x)\). The note contrasts irrational endpoints.
statement: For a full-level cusp form, the path integral from a rational cusp x to infinity converges, interpreted with cusp approach inside the upper half-plane, and is periodic in x. No uniform divergence claim for every irrational endpoint is needed.
reconstruction: The unqualified phrase about irrational points is retained as a heuristic, not a theorem with universal quantifier.
fate: \citet[\S3.2 and Proposition~9.2]{manin1973periods}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The period distribution relation
notes: \(\lambda_pP(x)=p^wP(px)+\sum_{a=0}^{p-1}P((x+a)/p)\).
statement: If \(T_p\Phi=a_p\Phi\), changing variables in the convergent cusp integrals gives \(\sum_{j=0}^{p-1}P((x+j)/p)=a_pP(x)-p^{k-2}P(px)\) for rational x.
fate: \citet[Proposition~9.2(d)]{manin1973periods}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The tentative correction of the period half-measure
notes: The page labelled correction has \(\rho^{-m}P(a/p^m)-p^w\rho^{-(m+m)}P(a/p^{m+1})\), with a manuscript question mark.
statement: For \(\rho^2-a_p\rho+p^{k-1}=0\), a compatible distribution at level n is \(\rho^{-n}P(a/p^n)-p^{k-2}\rho^{-n-1}P(a/p^{n-1})\). The next talk writes an overall \(\rho\)-multiple of this formula.
reconstruction: Both the second exponent and the direction of the denominator shift are repaired, using the explicit corrected repetition on P000509, not merely the printed formula.
fate: \citet[Lemma~9.4 and formula~(39)]{manin1973periods}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The corrected quadratic-root distribution
notes: For a root \(\rho\) of \(\rho^2-\lambda_p\rho+p^{w+1}=0\), the notes assign \(\rho^{-m}P(a/p^{m+1})-p^w\rho^{-m-1}P(a/p^m)\) to a class modulo \(p^{m+1}\).
statement:
For every n≥1, let \(
u_n(a)=ho^{1-n}P(a/p^n)-p^{k-2}ho^{-n}P(a/p^{n-1})\). The Hecke distribution relation and the quadratic equation imply \(\sum_{j=0}^{p-1}
u_{n+1}(a+jp^n)=
u_n(a)\). This gives a complex-valued finitely additive distribution before period normalization.
reconstruction: \(n=m+1\) and \(k=w+2\) reconcile indexing. A nonzero root is automatic since \(p^{k-1}\ne0\).
fate: \citet[Lemma~9.4 and formula~(39)]{manin1973periods}, up to the stated overall factor \(\rho\).
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Periods and critical L-values
notes: \(\tau_j(\Phi)=\int_0^{i\infty}\Phi(z)z^jdz\), and \(\tau_j=j!i^{j+1}L_\Phi(j+1)/(2\pi)^{j+1}\).
statement: For a weight \(k=w+2\) cusp form and \(0\le j\le k-2\), its period is \(\tau_j=i^{j+1}\Gamma(j+1)(2\pi)^{-j-1}L(f,j+1)\). The critical integers are \(1,\ldots,k-1\). The completed L-function satisfies its functional equation about \(s=k/2\).
reconstruction: The notebook\textquoteright s phrase critical strip means the critical integer range, not the analytic critical strip of a Dirichlet series.
fate: \citet[\S1.1--1.2]{manin1973periods}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Continued fractions and integral modular-symbol reduction
notes: Consecutive convergents give matrices \(g_j\in SL_2(\mathbb Z)\); the path from 0 to b/d is cut into transformed standard paths.
statement: For rational b/d and weight k, Euclidean-algorithm edges join adjacent cusps of determinant ±1. Changing variables under the corresponding modular matrices expresses \(P(b/d)\) as \(\sum_{j=0}^{k-2}A_j(b/d)\tau_j\) with \(A_j\in\mathbb Z\), after consistent path orientations.
reconstruction: The initial edge and its orientation repair the first sum\textquoteright s lower index 0, which otherwise invokes an undefined convergent -1.
fate: \citet[Proposition~3.2 and Proposition~9.2(c)]{manin1973periods}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Parity and reality of periods
notes: Even-index periods are purely imaginary and odd-index periods real.
statement: If the cusp form has real Fourier coefficients, then \(f(iy)\in\mathbb R\) and \(\tau_j=i^{j+1}\int_0^\infty f(iy)y^jdy\); thus even j gives an imaginary period and odd j a real period.
reconstruction: The real-coefficient hypothesis is necessary and appears on the following page.
fate: \citet[Proposition~9.2, proof]{manin1973periods}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Algebraicity after two period normalizations
notes: There exist \(\omega^+,\omega^-\) such that the even and odd period ratios lie in the field of Fourier coefficients.
statement: For a nonzero normalized simultaneous Hecke eigenform \(f\in S_k(SL_2(\mathbb Z))\) and its coefficient field E, there are nonzero complex numbers \(\Omega^+,\Omega^-\) for which \(\tau_j/\Omega^+\in E\) for even j and \(\tau_j/\Omega^-\in E\) for odd j.
reconstruction: Normalization, eigenform and nonzero-period hypotheses are explicit. The theorem does not prove that the common factors themselves are transcendental.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1.2]{manin1973periods}; submitted in 1973 after the earlier-year seminar exposition.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Eichler-Shimura period relations
notes: The order-two and order-three modular generators give two families of homogeneous period equations, including \(\tau_j+(-1)^j\tau_{w-j}=0\).
statement: For even w, the period polynomial \(r_f(X)=\int_0^{i\infty}f(z)(z-X)^w dz\) satisfies \(r_f|(1+S)=0\) and \(r_f|(1+U+U^2)=0\), using the right weight-w polynomial action of the order-two and order-three elements of PSL2(Z). Expanding gives the notebook\textquoteright s linear relations.
reconstruction: Polynomial-action conventions make the signs unambiguous; they are not a new conjecture.
fate: \citet[\S2, equations~(4)--(5)]{manin1973periods}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Odd period coordinates and the one-dimensional even excess
notes: The real cusp-form space maps isomorphically onto \(S^-\), and into \(S^+\) with codimension one.
statement: For even \(k\ge4\), the odd period-polynomial solution space has the same real dimension as the space of real-coefficient cusp forms, and the even solution space contains their period image with one-dimensional Eisenstein/coboundary excess. The period maps have the stated injectivity and isomorphism properties.
reconstruction: The standard period-polynomial conventions and weight range are supplied; this assertion is not about arbitrary cohomology of all modular forms.
fate: \citet[\S2, Proposition~2.3]{manin1973periods}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Hecke operators on period coordinates
notes: A commutative diagram transfers \(T_p\) to \(T_p^-\), with arithmetic matrix entries. The rewritten analytic formula has a minus sign before the average.
statement: The Hecke action on the odd period image is induced by an integral matrix in the standard period coordinates; the period map intertwines it with the usual plus-sign Hecke operator on cusp forms.
reconstruction: The minus sign in the analytic formula is a notebook error, contradicted by its own P000507 formula and Fourier recurrence.
fate: \citet[Proposition~3.2]{manin1973periods}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Ramanujan congruence modulo 691
notes: The discriminant form\textquoteright s coefficients satisfy \(\tau(n)\equiv\sum_{d\mid n}d^{11}\pmod{691}\).
statement: For \(\Delta(q)=q\prod_{m\ge1}(1-q^m)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n\), the congruence \(\tau(n)\equiv\sigma_{11}(n)\pmod{691}\) holds for every n≥1.
reconstruction: The statement was already known; a new proof mechanism is not a new open problem.
fate: \citet[\S1.3 and \S7]{manin1973periods} supplies a period-based proof of the older congruence.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Algebraic normalized period measures
notes: \(P^+=i\operatorname{Im}P/\omega^+\) and \(P^-=\operatorname{Re}P/\omega^-\) are used in the corrected measure formula.
statement: Choose parity periods as above. The rational-cusp values of the normalized even and odd components lie in a fixed number field with bounded denominators. After fixing an embedding into \(\overline{\mathbb Q}_p\) and a finite completion containing \(\rho\), the compatible distribution is p-adic valued.
reconstruction: The choice of complex parity convention, number-field embedding and completion is indispensable.
fate: \citet[Proposition~9.2(c), \S9.3--9.5]{manin1973periods}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The ordinary root gives a bounded measure
notes: If \(\lambda_p\) is coprime to p, one root gives a bounded measure and the other a growing one.
statement: Normalize \(v_p(p)=1\). If \(a_p\) is a p-adic unit, the roots of \(X^2-a_pX+p^{k-1}\) have valuations 0 and k−1. The unit root in the bounded-denominator distribution formula gives a bounded measure. The other root has a potentially growing upper bound; boundedness cannot be excluded merely from that bound.
reconstruction: The root valuations and positive conclusion are exact. The assertion that every nonunit-root distribution must grow needs a noncancellation hypothesis.
fate: \citet[\S9.5]{manin1973periods}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The unresolved relation between a_p and p
notes: \ru{Неизв. связь} \(\lambda_p\) \ru{и} \(p\), after the ordinary-prime discussion.
statement: The record does not specify whether it asks for a fixed-prime criterion, infinitely many ordinary primes, their density, or a uniform bound. These are different arithmetic questions.
fate: \citet[\S9.5]{manin1973periods} discusses growth, but does not supply missing quantifiers for this remark.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: no definite question can be indexed without strengthening the notebook.

title: Primitive-character interpolation of the critical value at one
notes: The notebook writes \(\int\chi\,d\mu_f^\pm=\cdots L_f(1,\chi)\), leaving constants as dots.
statement: For a normalized full-level eigenform, choose compatible periods, a p-adic embedding and a root \(\rho\). For primitive Dirichlet characters of p-power conductor, the distribution\textquoteright s finite character sums equal the period-normalized twisted critical value at s=1, with the conductor power of \(\rho\), Gauss sum, inverse-character convention and parity fixed by the definition. Under moderate growth this is the restriction of an analytic Mellin transform.
reconstruction: No numerical prefactor is attributed to the notebook: its ellipses prevent a literal normalization match. Locally constant character sums exist even without a bounded measure.
fate: \citet[Theorem~10.2, formula~(40)]{manin1973periods} supplies the complete normalization. The notes alone do not determine their dots.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The Lichtenbaum regulator interpretation of zeta(3)
notes: \(\zeta(3)=2\pi^2|K_4\mathbb Z|e_5(\alpha_5)\), where \(\alpha_5\) generates the free part of \(K_5\mathbb Z\) and \(e_5\) is described only as a certain real homomorphism.
statement: The exact coefficient cannot be evaluated until a normalization and sign of \(e_5\) are given. A precise weaker modern statement is that the appropriate nonzero real regulator on \(K_5(\mathbb Z)/\mathrm{torsion}\) is related to \(\zeta(3)/\pi^2\) by a nonzero rational factor; it does not imply transcendence of either side.
reconstruction: The weaker Borel comparison is identified separately. It is not claimed to verify the exact notebook coefficient 2, nor to solve all modern special-value conjectures.
fate: \citet[\S4]{lichtenbaum1972values} is the historical conjectural setting; \citet[\S6.4]{borel1977zeta} establishes the regulator comparison up to rational factors, with its normalization explicitly defined.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the regulator framework is established, but the exact handwritten equality remains undernormalized.

title: Transcendence of zeta(3)
notes: \ru{Не док., что} \(\sum_{n\ge1}n^{-3}\) \ru{трансценд.}
statement: Is \(\zeta(3)=\sum_{n\ge1}n^{-3}\) transcendental over \(\mathbb Q\)?
fate: Ap\'ery proved irrationality in 1978; \citet[\S1, p.~2; manuscript dated 26 October 2024]{nica2024irrationality} explicitly separates that theorem from the still-unknown transcendence question. A recent preprint, \citet[Theorem~1.6; v2 dated 15 October 2026]{lai2026linear}, reports linear independence of \(1,\zeta(3),\zeta(4)\). This is a strictly weaker arithmetic assertion and is not a proof of transcendence; its theorem statement and introduction, rather than the complete proof, were checked.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: irrationality is proved, while no accepted transcendence proof was identified in the literature search completed on this date.
worth: No bounded development is justified here: the precise transcendence problem remains far beyond the elementary estimates in these notes.

title: The arithmetic nature of Euler's constant
notes: Immediately after the transcendence sentence: \ru{Пост. Эйлера тоже не док.}
statement: Reading the carried-over predicate literally gives the question whether \(\gamma=\lim_{n\to\infty}(\sum_{j=1}^n1/j-\log n)\) is transcendental. The notebook does not separately distinguish irrationality from transcendence.
reconstruction: The antecedent of “also” is identified, but the weak notebook wording is preserved; no claim of a newly posed precise irrationality conjecture is made.
fate: \citet[Conjectures~1.0.1--1.0.2 and \S3]{lagarias2013euler} surveys the arithmetic problem; even irrationality remains unproved in the accepted results checked.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the checked literature gives partial arithmetic criteria, not a proof of irrationality or transcendence; no accepted later proof was identified.
worth: No bounded attack is justified by this one-line remark; it is useful as a historical occurrence of a familiar arithmetic question.

title: Wallach factorization through the Poisson bracket
notes: For a bilinear form \(B\) on polynomials, \(B(P_1(Q),P_2(Q))=0\) implies \(B(R,S)=L(\{R,S\})\). The inserted phrase specifies two variables, while the next line says any number.
statement: Let \(B:\mathbb C[x,y]\times\mathbb C[x,y]\to\mathbb C\) be bilinear and suppose \(B(p(q),r(q))=0\) for all \(p,r\in\mathbb C[t]\) and \(q\in\mathbb C[x,y]\). There is a unique linear functional \(L\) on \(\mathbb C[x,y]\) such that \(B(f,g)=L(f_xg_y-f_yg_x)\).
reconstruction: The polynomial ring and characteristic zero are fixed explicitly. The two-variable conclusion cannot be read as a theorem with an unspecified Poisson structure in an arbitrary number of variables.
fate: The algebraic form of Wallach\textquoteright s lemma is proved in \citet[\S4, algebraic preliminaries and Proposition~4.2]{heltonhowe1975traces}, extending the 1973 work. This is an exposition of the Helton--Howe programme, not a new theorem by the seminar speaker.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The Helton--Howe trace measure
notes: Boundedness is unstated: self-adjoint \(U,V\) commute modulo nuclear operators and \(\operatorname{Tr}[R(U,V),S(U,V)]=\iint\{R,S\}\,d\sigma\). The order of the factors is said to be immaterial.
statement: For bounded self-adjoint operators \(U,V\) on a complex separable Hilbert space with \([U,V]\) trace class, there is a finite, compactly supported, purely imaginary Borel measure \(\sigma\) on \(\mathbb R^2\) such that the displayed formula holds for all complex polynomials in two variables. Any fixed ordering convention gives the same trace of the commutator; it need not give the same operator.
reconstruction: Bounded operators and a complex measure remove domain and missing-factor ambiguities. Nuclear here means trace class.
fate: \citet[main theorem, formula~\((1^{\prime})\)]{heltonhowe1973integral}, presented at Halifax in April 1973 and printed in October. The ordering assertion is checked in \citet[Theorem~I and preceding paragraph]{heltonhowe1975traces}. The exact measure normalization is restated in \citet[Theorem~3.3]{sugahara2026heltonhowe}; its newer Toeplitz applications are not needed for the 1973 assertion.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Normed rings in a proposed p-adic operator theory
notes: After citing Douglas\textquoteright s book, the notes propose suitably chosen normed rings in the p-adic case in place of differential operators.
statement: No ring, module category, norm, class of operators or theorem to be recovered is specified. The strongest supported statement is a methodological suggestion linking the preceding operator theory to Manin\textquoteright s integration talks.
fate: The operator-algebra context is documented by \citet[Introduction]{heltonhowe1975traces}; comparison with \citet[Introduction]{manin1976nonarchimedean} does not identify a precise common construction.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: an unformulated programme; no mathematical problem is manufactured from it.

title: C*-extensions by the compact operators
notes: \(0\to\mathcal K\to\mathcal A\to C(X)\to0\), called an extension of Banach algebras; \(X\) is compact and \(\mathcal K\) acts on a separable Hilbert space.
statement: For nonempty compact metrizable \(X\) and an infinite-dimensional separable complex Hilbert space \(H\), consider essential C*-algebra extensions of \(C(X)\) by \(\mathcal K(H)\), with *-homomorphisms and the usual equivalence modulo addition of split extensions. In this category the resulting \(\operatorname{Ext}(X)\) is an abelian group.
reconstruction: C*-structure, metrizability, essentiality and stable equivalence replace the misleading unrestricted Banach-algebra wording.
fate: \citet{browndouglasfillmore1973unitary}; the definitions and chronology are checked in the authors\textquoteright s retrospective \citet[pp.~699--701]{douglas1980extensions}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Busby maps, splitting and addition
notes: Embeddings \(C(X)\hookrightarrow\mathcal L/\mathcal K\) are taken up to unitary equivalence; those lifting to \(\mathcal L\) are trivial. Addition is \(\tau_1\oplus\tau_2\) on \(H_1\oplus H_2\cong H\).
statement: An essential extension determines an injective *-homomorphism \(\tau:C(X)\to\mathcal Q(H)=\mathcal B(H)/\mathcal K(H)\), and its pullback recovers the extension. A *-homomorphic lift defines a split class. Direct sum, followed by a unitary identification of infinite-dimensional separable Hilbert spaces, gives the addition on Ext; stable equivalence makes the choice immaterial.
fate: \citet[p.~700]{douglas1980extensions} gives precisely these equivalent constructions and attributes the commutative case to the 1973 work.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Suspensions and the homological interpretation
notes: \(\operatorname{Ext}_{1-n}(X)=\operatorname{Ext}(S^nX)\); the main result is said to reduce Atiyah\textquoteright s \(\operatorname{Ell}(X)\) to Ext.
statement: For based finite CW complexes, reduced groups \(\widetilde E_{1-n}(X)=\operatorname{Ext}(\Sigma^nX)\) extend, with periodicity, to reduced complex K-homology. In particular \(\operatorname{Ext}(X)\cong K_1(X)\), whereas even Fredholm cycles represent \(K_0(X)\). The relation with Atiyah\textquoteright s Ell uses the even group and an equivalence relation on cycles; it is not literally \(\operatorname{Ell}(X)=\operatorname{Ext}_1(X)\).
reconstruction: Reduced suspensions, the even/odd degree distinction, and the cycle quotient are supplied. The result was announced in the BDF programme before this exposition; the 1977 proof date is not its first circulation.
fate: \citet[p.~702]{douglas1980extensions} distinguishes the two degrees and the solution of Atiyah\textquoteright s problem; the full treatment is \citet{browndouglasfillmore1977extensions}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Exact sequence for a closed subcomplex
notes: The sequence begins \(\operatorname{Ext}_1(A)\to\operatorname{Ext}_1(X)\to\operatorname{Ext}_1(X/A)\to\operatorname{Ext}_0(A)\).
statement: For a based finite CW pair \((X,A)\) with \(A\ne\varnothing\) a subcomplex, the reduced BDF homology groups have the cofiber long exact sequence \(\cdots\to\widetilde E_1(A)\to\widetilde E_1(X)\to\widetilde E_1(X/A)\to\widetilde E_0(A)\to\cdots\).
reconstruction: The finite CW-pair scope avoids treating an arbitrary inclusion as a cofiber sequence without qualifications.
fate: The generalized homology theorem in \citet[p.~702]{douglas1980extensions} supplies the exactness framework; \citet{browndouglasfillmore1977extensions} is the full original treatment.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The family index pairing
notes: \(K^1(X\times Y)\times\operatorname{Ext}_1(X)\to K^0(Y)\).
statement: For finite CW complexes \(X,Y\), an odd K-cohomology class over \(X\times Y\) and an extension class in \(K_1(X)\) give a class in \(K^0(Y)\): apply the Busby map to a matrix representative, lift to a continuous Fredholm family, and take its index bundle. For \(Y=\mathrm{pt}\) this is the integer Fredholm-index pairing.
reconstruction: Finite complexes, stabilized representatives and norm-continuous local lifts are needed for the family index; the compressed first line in the notebook does not fix degrees.
fate: The scalar pairing and the K-homology identification are checked in \citet[pp.~702--703]{douglas1980extensions}; the family refinement is a reconstruction of the explicit notebook formula, not a separately located theorem in the accessible 1973 text.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The garbled relation between Ext and degree-zero K-homology
notes: The boxed formula is transcribed \(\operatorname{Ext}_1\oplus\mathbb Z=K_0\) for simplicial complexes; the operation is overwritten, but the subscript 1 is visible in the scan.
statement: With the suspension convention on P000512, for a connected based finite CW complex \(X\) the correct degree-zero formula is \(\operatorname{Ext}(\Sigma X)\oplus\mathbb Z\cong K_0(X)\). It cannot be \(\operatorname{Ext}(X)\oplus\mathbb Z\): at \(X=S^1\) that would incorrectly identify \(\mathbb Z^2\) with \(\mathbb Z\).
reconstruction: This is a degree correction, not a proposed decipherment of the overwritten operation. The added summand is the unreduced basepoint summand.
fate: \citet[p.~702]{douglas1980extensions} explicitly identifies \(E_0(X)\) with \(K_0(X)\).
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The affine-group extension and two indices
notes: \(0\to\mathcal K\to C^*(ax+b)\to C(\infty)\to0\), \(\operatorname{Ext}(\infty)=\mathbb Z+\mathbb Z\); the notes ask for the pair for a specific operator.
statement: If the infinity-shaped symbol denotes the figure-eight graph \(S^1\vee S^1\), its Ext group is \(\mathbb Z^2\), with two index coordinates. But the group version of \(ax+b\), its representation, the precise ideal and the operator whose indices are requested are not recorded, so no numerical pair is determined.
reconstruction: The figure-eight interpretation is conditional. It is not substituted for the source symbol as an established transcription correction.
fate: The planar index classification in \citet[pp.~701--702]{douglas1980extensions} explains the graph interpretation. It does not identify this particular affine-group extension. The scan confirms an infinity-shaped symbol, not a written definition of the space.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the numerical question is underdetermined; no problem-index entry or claim of a remaining research problem is justified.

title: Extensions of the circle are classified by the index
notes: For \(X=\mathbb T\), the image \(T\) of the generator satisfies \(TT^*=1\bmod\mathcal K\); the answer is the index.
statement: A unital Busby map \(C(S^1)\to\mathcal Q(H)\) sends the coordinate function to a unitary in the Calkin algebra. Every lift \(T\) satisfies both \(TT^*-1\in\mathcal K\) and \(T^*T-1\in\mathcal K\), is Fredholm, and determines the extension by its index. Thus \(\operatorname{Ext}(S^1)\cong\mathbb Z\), with sign depending on the choice of generator.
reconstruction: The star homomorphism supplies the second unitary relation. A single displayed relation permits a coisometry whose kernel has infinite dimension. Such an operator is not Fredholm.
fate: \citet[pp.~701--702]{douglas1980extensions}; compare the equivalent normal-operator classification in \citet[Theorem~1.1 and following paragraph]{friisrordam2001approximation}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Normal operators plus compact operators form a closed set
notes: \(\{N+K:N\text{ normal},K\text{ compact}\}\) is norm closed.
statement: On an infinite-dimensional separable complex Hilbert space, the set of compact perturbations of bounded normal operators is closed in operator norm. Equivalently, an essentially normal operator belongs to it exactly when \(\operatorname{ind}(T-\lambda)=0\) for every \(\lambda\notin\sigma_{\rm ess}(T)\).
fate: The 1973 BDF result is reproved in \citet[Theorem~1.1 and \S2, proof of Theorem~1.1]{friisrordam2001approximation}; the primary article identifies BDF Corollary~11.2 as the original source.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The asserted failure of closure for pairs
notes: The circled insertion says that pairs \((N_1+K_1,N_2+K_2)\), with commuting normal \(N_1,N_2\), are not closed among pairs of this kind.
statement: One possible reading is nonclosure in \(\mathcal B(H)^2\) of compact perturbations of commuting bounded normal pairs. The notebook gives no example and its phrase ``all pairs of this kind leaves the ambient class unclear. This is kept separate from the verified one-operator theorem.
fate: Exact-phrase and BDF-title searches, the available 1973 metadata, \citet[pp.~699--704]{douglas1980extensions}, and \citet[\S2]{friisrordam2001approximation} did not locate the asserted pair counterexample. Neither the one-variable theorem nor general Ext theory alone verifies it.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: a recorded claim whose precise ambient hypotheses and primary counterexample remain unresolved in this audit; it is not classified as an unsolved research problem.

title: Simplicial objects and the simplex category
notes: A simplicial object is a contravariant functor from Ord, whose morphisms are nondecreasing maps of \(\{0,\ldots,p\}\) to \(\{0,\ldots,q\}\).
statement: Let \(\Delta\) have objects \([n]=\{0,\ldots,n\}\), \(n\ge0\), and order-preserving maps. A simplicial object in a category \(\mathcal S\) is a functor \(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S\). The elementary injections omit one vertex; the elementary surjections identify adjacent vertices.
fate: \citet[\S1, p.~105]{segal1968classifying}; \citet[\S1]{quillen1973higher}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The face and degeneracy presentation
notes: The two ladders have \(q+1\) face and \(q+1\) degeneracy arrows; the relations are said to be easy to write down.
statement: The structure consists of \(d_i:S_n\to S_{n-1}\) and \(s_i:S_n\to S_{n+1}\), \(0\le i\le n\), subject to \(d_id_j=d_{j-1}d_i\) for \(i<j\), \(s_is_j=s_{j+1}s_i\) for \(i\le j\), and \(d_is_j=s_{j-1}d_i\) for \(i<j\), \(d_js_j=d_{j+1}s_j=1\), \(d_is_j=s_jd_{i-1}\) for \(i>j+1\).
reconstruction: The relations omitted by the notebook are supplied explicitly.
fate: This expands the functorial definition in \citet[\S1]{segal1968classifying}; no additional result is attributed to the speaker.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The singular simplicial set
notes: \(S_q\) is the set of continuous maps \(\Delta^q\to X\); the face maps restrict and the degeneracy maps precompose with affine projections.
statement: For a topological space \(X\), put \(\operatorname{Sing}(X)_q=C(\Delta^q,X)\), considered as a set. Precomposition with affine maps induced by \(\Delta\)-morphisms gives the simplicial structure. This is different from topologizing these function spaces as a simplicial space.
fate: The construction is an instance of \citet[\S1]{segal1968classifying}; the distinction between sets and spaces is explicit there.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Geometric realization and its CW cells
notes: The notebook glues copies of \(\Delta^q\) for the nondegenerate simplices and calls the result a cell space.
statement: For a simplicial set \(S\), \(|S|=(\coprod_{q\ge0}S_q\times\Delta^q)/\sim\), where \((S(\alpha)s,t)\sim(s,\alpha_*t)\). This is a CW complex with one open q-cell for each nondegenerate q-simplex. Attaching maps may identify boundary points and may map a face through a lower-dimensional degeneracy.
reconstruction: The all-simplices quotient avoids the notebook\textquoteright s incorrect assumption that every face of a nondegenerate simplex stays nondegenerate.
fate: \citet[\S1, p.~105]{segal1968classifying}; \citet[\S1, realization preliminaries]{quillen1973higher}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Faces of nondegenerate simplices can be degenerate
notes: The handwritten sentence says that arrows from right to left take nondegenerate simplices to nondegenerate simplices.
statement: This is false for general simplicial sets. In the nerve of the group \(C_2=\{1,g\}\), the 2-simplex \((g,g)\) is nondegenerate, but its middle face is \(g^2=1\), the degenerate 1-simplex. Thus the page\textquoteright s own forthcoming group example supplies a counterexample.
reconstruction: The counterexample is editorial; the erroneous sentence is visibly in the scan and is not blamed on the transcription.
fate: The nerve and its degeneracies are defined in \citet[\S2--3]{segal1968classifying}. \ours\ The counterexample uses these definitions directly and was independently checked against the face and degeneracy formulas.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Realizing a simplicial space retains a topology
notes: The note says a topological structure no longer arises for simplicial topological spaces, because the pieces have product topologies.
statement: The same coend construction for a simplicial topological space has a quotient topology. What need not hold without additional conditions is the previous description as a CW complex with discrete cells indexed by simplices. If every level is a suitable compactly generated space, realization is taken in that category.
reconstruction: Replacing ``topological structure by ``the preceding cell structure is a mathematical emendation, not a reading supplied by the manuscript.
fate: \citet[\S1, p.~106]{segal1968classifying} explicitly defines realization of simplicial spaces.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The singular realization comparison
notes: For a good space, the realization of its singular complex is homotopy equivalent to the original space.
statement: The evaluation map \(|\operatorname{Sing}X|\to X\), sending a simplex and barycentric point to its value, is a weak homotopy equivalence. If \(X\) has the homotopy type of a CW complex, it is a homotopy equivalence.
reconstruction: ``Good is replaced by the explicit CW-type condition. No homotopy-equivalence assertion is made for arbitrary spaces.
fate: The usual comparison between realization and singular complexes underlies the constructions of classifying spaces in \citet[Chapter~IV, \S3]{weibel2013kbook}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: An ordered simplicial model of a polyhedron
notes: To reconstruct a polyhedron, the notes propose affine maps of simplices into it.
statement: For an ordered simplicial complex \(K\), use the simplicial set whose q-simplices are weakly increasing lists of vertices lying in one simplex, allowing repetitions. Its realization is canonically homeomorphic to \(|K|\). Arbitrary affine maps with arbitrary vertex images are a larger construction and do not give this finite combinatorial description.
reconstruction: The vertex-preserving and order-preserving restrictions are supplied.
fate: \citet[\S4, p.~108]{segal1968classifying} stresses the need to order vertices and the natural ordering of barycentric subdivision.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Realization of products and the topology convention
notes: \(\operatorname{real}(S\times S^{\prime})\to|S|\times|S^{\prime}|\) is asserted to be a homeomorphism.
statement: For simplicial sets the natural map is a homeomorphism when the target product is formed in compactly generated spaces. It is also a homeomorphism with the ordinary product in the standard finite cases used here. The unqualified statement with arbitrary ordinary topological products needs this restriction.
reconstruction: The notebook does not specify the category of spaces.
fate: \citet[\S1, p.~106]{segal1968classifying} and \citet[\S1, realization preliminaries]{quillen1973higher} state the k-space qualification.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The simplicial interval
notes: For the ordered segment, \(S_q\) has \(q+2\) elements, given by a switch from 0 to 1.
statement: \(\Delta[1]_q=\operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta}([q],[1])\) consists of the q+2 weakly increasing binary strings. There are two nondegenerate 0-simplices and one nondegenerate 1-simplex, and no others. Its realization is the closed interval.
fate: The interval-category construction in \citet[Proposition~2.1]{segal1968classifying} is exactly this model.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The nerve and classifying space of a small category
notes: \((NC)_q\) is the set of composable strings of q morphisms; faces discard endpoints or compose arrows, and degeneracies insert identities.
statement: For a small category \(C\), \((NC)_q=\operatorname{Fun}([q],C)\) and \(BC=|NC|\). For \(0<i<q\), \(d_i\) composes the arrows adjacent to \(X_i\); \(d_0,d_q\) delete the first or last object; \(s_i\) repeats \(X_i\) with its identity arrow.
fate: \citet[\S2]{segal1968classifying}; \citet[\S1]{quillen1973higher}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Groups as one-object categories and the C2 example
notes: A group is a one-object category, \((NG)_q=G^q\). For \(G=\mathbb Z_2\), there is one nondegenerate simplex in each dimension and the realization is \(\mathbb RP^{\infty}\).
statement: For a discrete group \(G\), \(BG\) is a \(K(G,1)\). For \(C_2\), a string is nondegenerate exactly when none of its entries is the identity, so there is one open cell in each dimension. Its realization has the homotopy type of \(\mathbb RP^{\infty}\), the standard classifying space for \(C_2\).
reconstruction: The robust comparison is stated up to homotopy; the notebook does not construct a specific homeomorphism of CW models.
fate: \citet[\S3]{segal1968classifying}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The first definition of the Q-construction and higher K-groups
notes: An abelian category or an extension-closed full subcategory \(M\) gives a category \(QM\) of spans and \(K_i(M)=\pi_{i+1}(BQM)\).
statement: Let \(M\) be an essentially small exact category. The objects of \(QM\) are those of \(M\); a morphism \(X\to Y\) is an isomorphism class of spans \(X\leftarrow E\to Y\) whose left map is an admissible epimorphism and right map an admissible monomorphism. Composition is by pullback. With basepoint the zero object, \(K_i(M)=\pi_{i+1}(BQM,0)\), \(i\ge0\).
reconstruction: Admissibility, middle-object isomorphism and the basepoint are made explicit; record 311 gives the detailed occurrence.
fate: \citet[\S2, pp.~99--103]{quillen1973higher}. The manuscript was prepared in early 1973; this is an exposition of it.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The product of two simplicial intervals
notes: The notes list the nondegenerate simplices of \(\Delta[1]\times\Delta[1]\), draw a diagonal square, and give a four-column array for the two triangles.
statement: A q-simplex is a pair of increasing maps \([q]\to[1]\); it is degenerate exactly when both maps repeat the same adjacent pair. There are four nondegenerate vertices, five nondegenerate edges and two nondegenerate triangles, giving the usual triangulation of \([0,1]^2\). No simplex of larger dimension is nondegenerate.
reconstruction: The four columns are read as two consecutive two-column triangles; no extra 2-simplices are inferred.
fate: This directly instantiates the product-realization construction of \citet[\S1]{segal1968classifying}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The nerve revisited
notes: The definition \(BC=\operatorname{Real}NC\) is repeated, with objects, nonidentity arrows and commutative triangles as its first cells.
statement: For a small category, the nondegenerate q-simplices are composable q-tuples of nonidentity arrows. Composite arrows occurring as faces may be identities; this does not alter nondegeneracy of the original tuple.
fate: \citet[\S2]{segal1968classifying}; compare the correction in item 1973-308.5.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Barycentric subdivision as a nerve
notes: Barycentric subdivision of a polyhedron of high degree is said to be the nerve of a category.
statement: For any simplicial complex \(K\), the poset of its nonempty simplices ordered by face inclusion is a small category; its nerve realizes to the barycentric subdivision of \(K\), hence to \(|K|\). No high-dimensional or repeated-subdivision hypothesis is needed.
reconstruction: The face-poset category identifies the unnamed category; the unclear phrase about degree is not treated as a necessary mathematical condition.
fate: \citet[\S4, p.~108]{segal1968classifying}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Natural transformations induce homotopies
notes: \(B(C\times C^{\prime})=BC\times BC^{\prime}\). A natural transformation \(f\Rightarrow g\) is a functor \(C\times\{0\to1\}\to C^{\prime}\), hence a homotopy.
statement: In compactly generated spaces, the classifying-space functor preserves finite products. A natural transformation determines \(BC\times[0,1]\to BC^{\prime}\), restricting to \(Bf\) and \(Bg\). For this interval product the usual topology already suffices.
reconstruction: The category \(\{0\to1\}\) is distinguished from its realized interval.
fate: \citet[Proposition~2.1 and following remark]{segal1968classifying}; \citet[\S1, Proposition~2]{quillen1973higher}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Initial and terminal objects give contractions
notes: If \(C\) has an initial or terminal object, \(BC\) is contractible; it is called a cone.
statement: A small category with an initial or terminal object has contractible classifying space. The unique arrows give a natural transformation between the identity and the corresponding constant functor, hence a contraction.
reconstruction: Contractibility is the invariant conclusion; a literal identification with a particular topological cone is unnecessary.
fate: \citet[\S1, Corollary~2 to Proposition~2]{quillen1973higher}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Adjoints give homotopy equivalences
notes: A functor with a left or a right adjoint induces a homotopy equivalence.
statement: If \(F:C\to D\) has either adjoint \(G\), the unit and counit induce homotopies showing \(BF\) and \(BG\) to be homotopy inverses.
fate: \citet[\S1, Corollary~1 to Proposition~2]{quillen1973higher}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Opposite categories have the same classifying space
notes: \(BC^{\circ}=BC\).
statement: For a small category, reversing each composable string and reversing its barycentric coordinates defines a canonical homeomorphism \(B(C^{\mathrm{op}})\cong BC\). This does not assert that the nerves are naturally isomorphic as simplicial sets.
reconstruction: Equality is replaced by the actual canonical homeomorphism.
fate: \citet[\S1, opposite-category construction]{quillen1973higher}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The homotopy sequence of a fibration
notes: The homotopy sequence of a Serre fibration is written, with an unmatched parenthesis in the fiber term.
statement: For a pointed Serre fibration \(f:(X,x)\to(Y,y)\) with fiber \(F=f^{-1}(y)\), there is the exact sequence \(\cdots\to\pi_q(F,x)\to\pi_q(X,x)\to\pi_q(Y,y)\to\pi_{q-1}(F,x)\to\cdots\); in low degrees it is an exact sequence of pointed sets with the usual action interpretation.
reconstruction: Basepoints and the low-degree qualification are supplied.
fate: This is the standard homotopy-fiber convention used by \citet[\S1, Theorem~B]{quillen1973higher}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Mapping paths replace an arbitrary map by a fibration
notes: \(\widetilde X=\{(x,s):s(0)=f(x)\}\), \(\widetilde f(x,s)=s(1)\), and \(\widetilde X\simeq X\).
statement: For a continuous map between compactly generated spaces, give the path space the compact-open k-topology. The inclusion using constant paths \(X\to\widetilde X\) is a homotopy equivalence, and endpoint evaluation \(\widetilde f\) is a fibration. Its fiber at \(y\) is the homotopy fiber of \(f\).
reconstruction: The path-space topology is stated explicitly.
fate: The construction fixes the homotopy-fiber meaning in \citet[\S1, Theorem~B]{quillen1973higher}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The comma-category map to the homotopy fiber
notes: \(Y\backslash g\) has pairs \((X,u:Y\to gX)\). On a simplex, adjoining \(Y\) produces a larger simplex in \(BC^{\prime}\), and a straight path supplies a point of the homotopy fiber.
statement: For a functor \(g:C\to D\) of small categories and \(Y\in D\), let \((Y\downarrow g)\) have objects \((X,u:Y\to gX)\) and arrows \(a:X\to X^{\prime}\) satisfying \(g(a)u=u^{\prime}\). Forgetting \(u\) gives a map to \(BC\), and the natural arrows from constant \(Y\) to \(gX\) give a canonical map \(B(Y\downarrow g)\to\operatorname{hofib}_Y(Bg)\).
reconstruction: The notebook uses a reversed chain convention on P000519; the natural-transformation description makes the path compatible with faces and degeneracies.
fate: \citet[\S1, pp.~93--97]{quillen1973higher}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Quillen Theorem B
notes: If every target arrow \(v:Y\to Y^{\prime}\) induces a homotopy equivalence \(B(Y^{\prime}\backslash g)\to B(Y\backslash g)\), the comma category models the homotopy fiber.
statement: Assume for every morphism \(v:Y\to Y^{\prime}\) in \(D\) that precomposition \(v^*:(Y^{\prime}\downarrow g)\to(Y\downarrow g)\) induces a homotopy equivalence on classifying spaces. Then \(B(Y\downarrow g)\to\operatorname{hofib}_Y(Bg)\) is a homotopy equivalence for every \(Y\), and yields the corresponding homotopy exact sequence.
fate: \citet[Theorem~B, p.~97]{quillen1973higher}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: A proposed limit over comma categories
notes: Fuchs suggests that \(Y\backslash g\) should probably be defined as an inverse limit over all such categories with different \(Y\).
statement: The notes do not specify an indexing category, the diagram, transition maps, ordinary versus homotopy limit, or the desired universal property. Theorem B already gives the precise assertion in the preceding item; this additional suggestion has no unique formal statement.
fate: Comparison with \citet[\S1, Theorem~B and its proof]{quillen1973higher} does not identify an additional theorem with these quantifiers.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: an exploratory comment, not a separate unresolved problem.

title: Fredholm representations of a ring with involution
notes: \(\Lambda\) has involution, \(T_1,T_2\) act on Hilbert spaces, \(F\) is Fredholm, and \(FT_1(\lambda)-T_2(\lambda)F\) is compact for every \(\lambda\).
statement: For a unital *-ring \(\Lambda\), a Fredholm representation consists of unital *-representations \(T_i:\Lambda\to\mathcal B(H_i)\) on separable complex Hilbert spaces and a bounded Fredholm operator \(F:H_1\to H_2\), such that \(FT_1(\lambda)-T_2(\lambda)F\) is compact for every \(\lambda\in\Lambda\). For \(\Lambda=\mathbb Z[\pi]\), this is equivalently a pair of unitary group representations with a compact-intertwining Fredholm operator.
reconstruction: Boundedness, complex Hilbert spaces and preservation of involution are explicit.
fate: \citet[Definition~1.1]{mishchenko1974infinite}; the paper was submitted December 1972 and its central construction was announced in 1973. The notebook generalizes the definition from group rings to *-rings. The public pre-talk announcement is \citet[\S\S1--3, p.~239]{mishchenko1973infinite}, published in the March--April 1973 issue and received 10 October 1972.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.
speaker: A. S. Mishchenko

title: Twisting a Fredholm cycle by a vector bundle
notes: For \(\Lambda=C(M)\), the notes write \(F\otimes1_\eta\) on \(H_i\otimes_{C(M)}\Gamma(\eta)\), then take the index.
statement: For compact \(M\), represent a vector bundle \(\eta\) by a projection \(e\in M_n(C(M))\). The compressed operator \(T_2(e)F^{(n)}T_1(e):T_1(e)H_1^n\to T_2(e)H_2^n\) is Fredholm. Its index defines an additive homomorphism \(K^0(M)\to\mathbb Z\). Because F intertwines only modulo compacts, the naive balanced tensor operator need not be literally well defined.
reconstruction: Projection compression makes the shorthand tensor construction precise and avoids treating a compactly intertwining operator as an exact module homomorphism.
fate: The Fredholm-cycle pairing is recalled in \citet[p.~702]{douglas1980extensions}; the family-index formalism is in \citet[\S2]{atiyahsinger1971families}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.
speaker: A. S. Mishchenko

title: Integer-valued pairings lose torsion information
notes: The first pairing is called an element of \(K_0(M)\), then corrected as too crude because \(K^0(M)\) can have torsion.
statement: An integer-valued homomorphism annihilates torsion in \(K^0(M)\), and does not by itself specify every analytic K-homology class. The Fredholm cycle is the richer object; its numerical pairing is only one invariant.
reconstruction: The initial identification is not retained as a definition of K-homology; it is qualified by the notebook itself.
fate: The distinction between Fredholm cycles and their integer pairing is explicit in \citet[p.~702]{douglas1980extensions}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.
speaker: A. S. Mishchenko

title: Families refine the numerical index
notes: For every \(Y\), \(T\) defines \(\operatorname{index}_T:K^0(M\times Y)\to K^0(Y)\), and this is said to be an element of \(K_0(M)\).
statement: For compact finite CW complexes \(M,Y\), projection compression in a continuous family gives \(\operatorname{index}_T:K^0(M\times Y)\to K^0(Y)\), natural in Y. The Fredholm cycle defines an even analytic K-homology class, whose family pairings retain more structure than the numerical map at \(Y=\mathrm{pt}\).
reconstruction: Compact parameter spaces and the index-bundle construction are supplied. A full characterization of all natural transformations is not asserted.
fate: \citet[\S2, family-index construction]{atiyahsinger1971families}; \citet[p.~702]{douglas1980extensions} gives the cycle interpretation.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.
speaker: A. S. Mishchenko

title: Elliptic symbols and analytic K-homology
notes: An elliptic operator has symbol in \(K^0(T^*M)\), compact commutators with functions, and K-homology class dual to its symbol.
statement: For a closed smooth manifold M and a bounded order-zero elliptic pseudodifferential operator between complex vector bundles, commutators with multiplication by smooth functions are of negative order and compact on L2. It therefore determines an even Fredholm cycle. The symbol lies in compactly supported \(K_c^0(T^*M)\); under the symbol/analytic K-homology identification, its image is this cycle. A positive-order differential operator first requires a bounded transform or Sobolev normalization.
reconstruction: Compact supports, a closed manifold and bounded normalization are essential; the statement is not ordinary untwisted K-cohomological Poincare duality on an arbitrary manifold.
fate: The symbol and family-index conventions are checked in \citet[Introduction and \S2]{atiyahsinger1971families}; the Fredholm-cycle framework is in \citet[p.~702]{douglas1980extensions}. The full duality identification is used here as the modern formulation of the notebook\textquoteright s Poincare-duality shorthand.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.
speaker: A. S. Mishchenko

title: The K-class of a Fredholm representation of a discrete group
notes: For \(\Lambda=\mathbb Z[\pi]\), a Fredholm representation determines \(\xi_T\in K^0(B\pi)\). The notebook gives the equivariant construction on the universal cover.
statement: For a discrete group \(\pi\) and a CW model of \(B\pi\), choose on each orbit of vertices of \(E\pi\) the operator F and extend equivariantly by \(\widehat F(gx)=T_2(g)\widehat F(x)T_1(g)^{-1}\). All values differ by compacts; barycentric interpolation on simplices stays Fredholm and gives an equivariant norm-continuous family. It descends between Hilbert bundles over \(B\pi\). Trivializing them gives a class in representable \(K^0(B\pi)\), independent of the choices.
reconstruction: For an infinite CW complex the K-group is representable K-theory. The stability of the Fredholm set under compact perturbations justifies each interpolation.
fate: \citet[\S2, Lemma~2.1 and pp.~86--87]{mishchenko1974infinite}. The construction itself works beyond the finitely presented groups emphasized in that paper; the 1973 announcement predates this intervention. The public pre-talk announcement is \citet[\S\S1--3, p.~239]{mishchenko1973infinite}, published in the March--April 1973 issue and received 10 October 1972.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.
speaker: A. S. Mishchenko

title: The Fredholm space has one component for each index
notes: The notes use \(K(B\pi)=[B\pi,BU]\) and \(BU\simeq\mathcal F\), where \(\mathcal F\) is all Fredholm operators.
statement: For infinite-dimensional separable complex H with the norm topology, \(\mathcal F(H)\simeq\mathbb Z\times BU\). The zero-index component alone has homotopy type BU. Consequently full K0 is represented by \(\mathbb Z\times BU\); reduced or fixed-index conventions must be stated to use BU alone.
reconstruction: The missing integer component is an emendation. A general F in the notebook is not assumed to have index zero.
fate: The family-index description in \citet[Introduction and \S2]{atiyahsinger1971families} and the Fredholm-family use in \citet[\S2]{mishchenko1974infinite} require the index components.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.
speaker: A. S. Mishchenko

title: Generalized signatures of Hermitian forms
notes: For an arbitrary ring with involution and an invertible Hermitian matrix A, the notes announce an integer \(\operatorname{sign}_T A\).
statement: Apply the two *-representations to an invertible Hermitian matrix \(A\in M_n(\Lambda)\). Their images are invertible self-adjoint operators; their positive and negative spectral subspaces are intertwined by \(F^{(n)}\) modulo compacts. The two diagonal compressions are Fredholm, and define \(\operatorname{sign}_T(A)=\operatorname{ind}F_+-\operatorname{ind}F_-\). For group rings this descends to the corresponding even Wall group in the stated signature degree.
reconstruction: The notebook gives no formula; the positive/negative spectral-compression formula is supplied from the paper. No analogous Wall-group descent for every unspecified *-ring is inferred.
fate: \citet[\S3, Definition~3.4 and Theorem~3.5]{mishchenko1974infinite} supplies the construction and its group-ring invariance. The public pre-talk announcement is \citet[\S\S1--3, p.~239]{mishchenko1973infinite}, published in the March--April 1973 issue and received 10 October 1972.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.
speaker: A. S. Mishchenko

title: The formal vector-field algebra and its filtration
notes: \(W_n=\sum_i k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]\partial_{x_i}\), with continuous inserted before derivations; \(\mathcal L_j\) is defined by degrees at least \(j+1\).
statement: Over a field k of characteristic zero, let \(\mathfrak m=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\) and \(W_n=\operatorname{Der}_{k,\rm cont} k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]\). For \(j\ge-1\), \(\mathcal L_j=\sum_i\mathfrak m^{j+1}\partial_{x_i}\). The order-of-vanishing filtration defines the linear topology; it is not the highest polynomial degree of a formal series.
reconstruction: Characteristic zero and the meaning of degree for formal power series are supplied.
fate: \citet[\S1, pp.~836--838]{rudakov1974irreducible}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Continuity into a discrete countable-dimensional module
notes: The notes write \(\rho:\mathcal L\to\operatorname{Aut}E\), and require a neighborhood V with \(\rho(v)x=0\).
statement: A continuous Lie-algebra representation is a homomorphism \(\rho:\mathcal L\to\operatorname{End}_k(E)\) for a discrete, countable-dimensional vector space E such that every \(x\in E\) is killed by some \(\mathcal L_j\). Equivalently every orbit map is locally constant at zero.
reconstruction: Automorphisms is the wrong target for a Lie-algebra action: even the zero Lie element acts by the zero endomorphism, not an invertible map. The neighborhood quantifier means every v in V.
fate: \citet[Lemma~2.1, p.~839]{rudakov1974irreducible}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Inflation from a finite jet quotient followed by induction
notes: A representation of \(M/M^{\prime}\), with \(M^{\prime}\) of finite codimension, is inflated to M and induced to \(\mathcal L\); later M is \(\mathcal L_0\).
statement: For an open Lie subalgebra \(\mathcal L_0\), a continuous module V that factors through \(\mathcal L_0/\mathcal L_r\) inflates to \(\mathcal L_0\) and gives \(U(\mathcal L)\otimes_{U(\mathcal L_0)}V\). Under the stated countable-dimensional discrete hypotheses the induced representation is continuous. A finite-dimensional quotient algebra does not require V itself to be finite-dimensional.
reconstruction: The abstract M in the opening programme is specialized to the open filtered subalgebra used in the theorem. No finite-dimensional-module hypothesis is added.
fate: \citet[Definitions~2.2--2.3 and following observation, pp.~839--840]{rudakov1974irreducible}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Minimal height and the kernel submodule
notes: \(p(x)=\min\{r:\mathcal L_rx=0\}\), \(\bar p(E)=\min_{x\ne0}p(x)\), and \(E_0=\{x:p(x)=\bar p(E)\}\) is asserted to be a submodule.
statement: For nonzero x define p(x) by its annihilator in the filtration. Let h be the minimum over nonzero vectors. Then \(E_0=\{0\}\cup\{x\ne0:p(x)=h\}\) is a \(\mathcal L_0\)-submodule. Indeed p(x+y) is at most the maximum of the two heights, and \([\mathcal L_0,\mathcal L_h]\subseteq\mathcal L_h\).
reconstruction: The printed paper explicitly adjoins zero; the notebook set omits it. The short argument here is a critical verification of the definition, not a new classification result.
fate: \citet[Definition~3.1, Proposition~3.2 and Corollary~3.3, p.~840]{rudakov1974irreducible}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: Irreducibility and reconstruction above height one
notes: If \(\bar p(E)>1\), the representation is induced: \(E=\operatorname{Ind}(E_0)\); the handwritten bound is retraced.
statement: For a Cartan-type algebra \(\mathcal L\) in Rudakov\textquoteright s filtration, every irreducible discrete continuous module E of height greater than one has irreducible \(\mathcal L_0\)-kernel \(E_0\), and \(U(\mathcal L)\otimes_{U(\mathcal L_0)}E_0\to E\) is an isomorphism. Conversely induction of an irreducible \(\mathcal L_0\)-module of height greater than one is irreducible.
reconstruction: The primary paper resolves the provisional bound as 1. Continuity, irreducibility, topology and filtration are inherited from the preceding definitions; the assertion is not about all abstract Wn-modules.
fate: \citet[Theorem~6.1 and Corollaries~6.2--6.3, pp.~843--844]{rudakov1974irreducible}; the manuscript was received six days before this talk and appeared in 1974.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The differential-form exceptions for W_n
notes: The opening says all irreducibles are induced with finitely many exceptions; the closing identifies \((d\Omega^p)^*\).
statement: For \(W_n\), the exceptional height-one inducing \(\mathcal L_0\)-modules are the n modules inflated from the \(\mathfrak{gl}_n\)-modules with highest weights \((0,\ldots,0,-1,\ldots,-1)\), having p entries equal to \(-1\), \(1\le p\le n\). Each exceptional induced module has a unique maximal proper submodule; its irreducible quotient is the continuous dual of \(d\Omega^{p-1}\), the formal exact p-forms. Other irreducible height-one inducing modules give irreducible induced modules.
reconstruction: The exact height-one statement is given instead of extending the shorthand to all unrestricted module categories. The dual is the continuous dual of the linearly compact formal-form space, hence discrete; the trivial representation is separately understood. Closed positive-degree formal forms are exact in characteristic zero.
fate: \citet[Definition~13.6, Theorem~13.7 and Corollaries~13.8--13.9, pp.~865--866]{rudakov1974irreducible}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The corresponding Hamiltonian result
notes: The last line says there are corresponding results for Hamiltonian ones as well.
statement: For \(H_{2m}\), using its induced formal filtration, the same high-height induction and irreducibility statements hold. The notebook does not state a list of height-one Hamiltonian exceptions.
reconstruction: Only the precise high-height assertion supported by the paper is identified. The Wn exceptional list is not transferred to the Hamiltonian algebra.
fate: \citet[\S1 and Theorem~6.1, Corollaries~6.2--6.3]{rudakov1974irreducible} explicitly includes H alongside W, S and K. The subsequent height-one classification for Hamiltonian algebras is \citet[Definition~5.5, Corollary~5.9 and Theorem~5.10, pp.~477--480]{rudakov1975types}, over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero; received 7 October 1974 and published in 1975. This supplies later fate, without attributing that complete exceptional list to the one-line 1973 remark.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope.

title: The parenthetical bounded-representation question
notes: \ru{\(\exists\) ли огр. непр. предст-я?} appears inside the discussion of height.
statement: The abbreviation may ask about a bounded height, bounded operators under a norm, or another boundedness condition. No norm, common height bound or quantified class is specified.
fate: \citet[\S\S2--3]{rudakov1974irreducible} defines continuity and height but does not determine the missing predicate of this parenthetical question.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: not sufficiently definite to receive a research-problem identifier.

title: Kirillov on finite-functional-dimension diffeomorphism representations
notes: Kirillov asks for representations of \(\operatorname{Diff}M\) of finite functional dimension, induced from a finite-point stabilizer modulo a finite-jet stabilizer; the note says unproved but well known.
statement: Given finitely many points of a smooth manifold, their stabilizer has finite jet quotient groups from which one can form induced representations. The note does not specify the topology on Diff, the representation category, the definition of functional dimension, the allowed jet order or an equivalence relation; it therefore does not determine an exhaustive classification theorem.
